name: Wood
description: Cut and dried timber used for tools, structures, fuel, and repairs.

name: Metal Ingot
description: A workable bar smelted from common metal ore.

name: Steel Ingot
description: A hardened structural metal suited to tools, armor, and load-bearing fittings.

name: Wire
description: Flexible drawn metal used in traps, repairs, bindings, and electrical work.

name: Nails
description: A bundle of common metal fasteners.

name: Chain
description: Ten feet of linked metal chain, difficult to cut and useful for hauling or restraint.

name: Padlock
description: A sturdy keyed lock for a chest, gate, or length of chain.

name: Manacles
description: Locking metal restraints sized for a humanoid creature.

name: Piton
description: A metal spike hammered into stone as an anchor point.

name: Climbing Harness
description: A leather-and-rope harness that distributes weight during a fall.

name: Climbing Kit
description: A harness, rope fittings, pitons, and a compact hammer for difficult ascents.

name: Hammer
description: A balanced hand tool for driving fasteners and shaping material.

name: Crowbar
description: A reinforced lever for prying doors, lids, and damaged machinery.

name: Chisel
description: A narrow hardened tool for cutting stone, wood, or metal.

name: Hand Saw
description: A toothed blade for controlled cuts through timber and bone.

name: Tongs
description: Long metal grips for handling hot, dangerous, or contaminated objects.

name: Needle
description: A fine metal needle for sewing cloth, hide, and wounds.

name: Sewing Kit
description: Needles, thread, patches, and a small pair of shears.

name: Bucket
description: A handled vessel for carrying water, loose goods, or salvage.

name: Waterskin
description: A sealed leather pouch that holds a day's drinking water.

name: Sack
description: A simple cloth container for bulky supplies.

name: Wooden Chest
description: A reinforced chest for storing and transporting valuables.

name: Candle
description: A small steady light source that burns for roughly one hour.

name: Lantern
description: A shielded reusable light source fueled by oil.

name: Chalk
description: A pale marking stick useful for trails, diagrams, and warnings.

name: Bell
description: A small clear-toned bell used for alarms, signals, and simple traps.

name: Mirror
description: A hand mirror useful for signaling and looking around dangerous corners.

name: Magnifying Lens
description: A shaped lens for close inspection and focusing light.

name: Pole
description: A ten-foot wooden pole for probing floors, reaching objects, and improvising supports.

name: Ladder
description: A portable wooden ladder long enough to cross modest gaps or reach high ledges.

name: Bedroll
description: Padded cloth bedding for an uncomfortable but restorative rest.

name: Blanket
description: A heavy woven blanket that protects against cold and can be repurposed in emergencies.

name: Tent
description: A compact two-person shelter with cloth walls, rope stays, and wooden poles.

name: Soap
description: A cleansing block useful for hygiene and removing mundane contaminants.

name: Bandage
description: Clean strips of cloth for controlling bleeding and protecting wounds.

name: Healer's Kit
description: Bandages, splints, needles, and common stabilizing supplies.

name: Caltrops
description: A pouch of four-pointed metal spikes used to slow pursuit.

name: Ball Bearings
description: A pouch of smooth metal spheres useful in machinery or as a floor hazard.

name: Signal Whistle
description: A piercing whistle audible over machinery and combat.

name: Spyglass
description: A compact optical tube for examining distant chambers and structures.

name: Hourglass
description: A glass timer useful for rituals, watches, and measured processes.

name: Quill
description: A cut feather used for precise writing and notation.

name: Journal
description: A bound blank book for recording routes, lexicon discoveries, and warnings.

name: Map Case
description: A waterproofed tube that protects papers and recovered diagrams.
